private_note: My income is the lowest fifth's income, full stop. Hazel gives me 41, Birch 36, Alder 32, Today 22, Cedar 15. Hazel nearly doubles what I live on. But 9 of 12 is a high bar and the top groups lose a lot under Hazel and Birch. If those can't reach 9, Alder is still a real gain over today, so I'll stay open to it in later rounds. statement: I work temp warehouse shifts. My hours change every week, I have no savings, and I'm a few credits short of a degree I can't afford to finish. I'm in the bottom fifth now and I'll be there under every plan, so I'll be straight with you: I'm voting for what my household lives on. Hazel takes us from 22 to 41. That's the gap between missing rent and being able to plan a year ahead. Birch and Alder also help, and I'd much rather see one of them pass than walk away with nothing. Cedar cuts us to 15 and drops health coverage for people like me, so I'll vote against it to the end. We need nine votes, and the convention won't meet again. Today's numbers are what we get if we deadlock. I'm open to a deal, but it has to leave the bottom clearly better off than it is now.
